thread.title: GE's John Flannery Is In The News Again: Stock Price Down 7.3% - General Electric Company (NYSE:GE)

author: John M. Mason
title: GE's John Flannery Is In The News Again: Stock Price Down 7.3% - General Electric Company (NYSE:GE)
text:
John Flannery, the CEO of General Electric (NYSE: GE ), cannot catch a break these days.
Mr. Flannery spoke at the Electric Products Group conference yesterday and, according to Thomas Gryta in the Wall Street Journal , his “comments disappointed Wall Street, which pushed GE’s shares down 7.3 percent in Wednesday trading to $14.18.
Mr. Flannery “reminded” participants at the conference “that major changes at the conglomerate will take some time.”
He followed up this remark with the statement: “This in not going to be a quick fix.”
Mr. Gryta commented
“Investors have waited since last summer for answers on the company’s direction, including a possible breakup. Mr. Flannery didn’t commit to a timeline for sharing his ultimate road map.”
In other words, Mr. Flannery has yet to give us his vision of what the future of General Electric looks like.
I argued, at the beginning of November last year: “GE’s CEO, John Flannery, Faces Crucial ‘Vision’ Day.” That crucial ‘vision’ day was November 13 at a meeting GE labeled as “Key Investor Update.”
“John Flannery, CEO of General Electric, is facing an existential moment on November 13, 2017. That day, General Electric is facing the investment community, promising on that date that Mr. Flannery will lay out the 'new' future of the giant company.”
“Mr. Flannery cannot change things at General Electric overnight. But Mr. Flannery must come out of the November 13 performance as a credible leader of General Electric. But to achieve this credibility, he has a lot of explaining to do.”
“Mr. Flannery, in the November 13 presentation, must come across as someone that is very credible. He only really gets one chance at this.”
Recent corporate experience has given us examples of how new CEOs need to perform .
The result for GE, however: “ GE's Flannery: A Lackluster Performance .”
And, since that date, he has been remarkably consistent in matching this performance.
The closest thing we have gotten as far as a vision for General Electric is that the company is to become “simpler” and “leaner.” There has been little detail added to this picture.
There has been little or no discussion of the role that GE will play in the digital future.
Why might a discussion of this area be important?
Well, there has been discussion recently that Apple (NASDAQ: AAPL ) might become “ The Epitome of Where the Modern Corporation is Going .” This is perhaps something that General Electric should consider in its future.
Guess what? General Electric has considered the Apple model and has already made moves in that direction. In April 2017, I wrote about this move , made under the direction of Jeff Immelt, Mr. Flannery predecessor:
“I think that the greatest long-term impact of Mr. Immelt’s vision for GE will be the transformation of GE into a ‘digital-industrial’ company. Mr. Immelt wanted to bring GE into the forefront of industrial software and data analysis. He has overseen the hiring of thousands of engineers, computer scientists, and math experts to staff this approach.”
Elsewhere, I described the effort :
“So, Immelt set off to build a computer division within General Electric. And, he set out a goal…to make GE a top 10 software company in 2020. That is, GE would be up there with IBM (NYSE: IBM ) and Microsoft (NASDAQ: MSFT ).”
Furthermore, I wrote, “Immelt is moving the company into new areas. The emphasis being put on the software and digital technology areas is huge and will, I believe, be the real foundation block of the future General Electric.”
GE is “300,000 people collaborating across oceans and industries, and Digital Technology is the glue that holds us together. From high-profile corporate projects, to real-time work out in the field-digital at GE is all about finding creative ways of connecting technology, machines and people to make the world work better.
Digital technology is the foundation for GE as a Digital Industrial company. Digital technology combines the best of software and information technology and is critical to the future of GE. With more than 11,000 professionals in roughly 50 countries, digital technology is a major area of focus and investment across the company and is essential to maintaining our leadership, competitiveness and success."
“This world requires constant change and innovation. It requires shorter product cycles and it requires different administrative hierarchies. And it requires many software developers and startup leaders. This was a major reason for moving (the company headquarters) from to Boston, MA, from Fairfield, CN.
Key to the success of Apple, as I wrote in the earlier article, was its excellence in the use of intellectual capital, and that was what making GE into a Digital Industrial company was all about.
But I have seen little or no mention of this "vision" in anything Mr. Flannery has said or written. The picture of the world I get from Mr. Flannery is that of making the industrial giant, General Electric, into a “simpler” and “leaner” industrial conglomerate.
This, however, is not where the world seems to be heading . The world seems to be heading toward the model built by Apple, which means that if Mr. Flannery and General Electric just think about keeping General Electric as an industrial conglomerate that is “simpler” and “leaner” without incorporating the digital implications of modern information technology into the structure, then there is not much of a future left for General Electric.
In addition, I have a new market strategy for trading General Electric stock. If Mr. Flannery is expected to speak somewhere, sell General Electric stock short.
